w: Zurich's own Hausberg, 870 metres of Albis ridge with the whole city, the Zürichberg and the lake laid out below. The summit, Uto Kulm, carries a hotel, a lookout tower you pay a couple of francs to climb, and a 186-metre TV tower, both rebuilt in 1990. Ride up, take the view, walk back down.
s: Zurich's home mountain, and its cheapest view
_facts: Mountain in the Albis chain, rising to 870 m, part of the Swiss plateau
Summit Uto Kulm is in Stallikon; panoramic view over Zurich, Zürichberg and Lake Zurich
Known as the Hausberg of Zurich
Hotel Uto Kulm at the summit plus a lookout tower (access CHF 2, rebuilt 1990) and a 186 m TV tower (rebuilt 1990)

w: Wedged between the main station and Platzspitz park, this is the country's story gathered under one roof - part of the Musée Suisse Group and affiliated with the Federal Office of Culture. No detour required to find it: it sits exactly where the trains already bring you.
s: Switzerland's story, right by the station
_facts: Swiss National Museum (Landesmuseum), Zurich's history museum
Adjacent to Zürich Hauptbahnhof and Platzspitz park
Part of the Musée Suisse Group, affiliated with the Federal Office of Culture

w: Football's official museum, opened in 2016 across town from FIFA's own headquarters and built for a reported 500 million francs - a sum investigators have since queried for 'suspected criminal mismanagement.' The trophies and shirts on display are genuine; the accounting behind the building, allegedly, rather less so.
s: FIFA's shrine to itself, budget under investigation
_facts: Football museum operated by FIFA, opened 28 February 2016
Located across town from FIFA headquarters
Project cost over SFr500 million ($563m), under investigation for suspected criminal mismanagement

w: A private villa turned gallery for arms manufacturer Emil Georg Bührle's collection - paintings now suspected of being looted from Jewish owners under Nazi Germany, alongside a family history that includes his son's 1970 conviction for arms sales to apartheid South Africa. Beautiful pictures, uncomfortable provenance.
s: Great art, arms money, looted-art questions
_facts: Art museum in a villa adjoining Emil Georg Bührle's former home
Many works suspected of being looted from Jews by Nazi Germany
Son Dieter Bührle managed the foundation for decades and was sentenced in 1970 to 8 months (conditional) for supplying weapons to apartheid South Africa
In 2021 many works went on 20-year loan to the Kunsthaus Zürich extension

w: A wooded ridge above the city that somehow holds the zoo, FIFA's headquarters and a scatter of grand villas within one stretch of forest. Tram 6, the Rigiblick funicular and the Dolderbahn rack railway all climb different flanks of it, and the Rigiblick restaurant at the top has been pouring drinks since 1901.
s: One hill: a zoo, FIFA HQ, and a restaurant since 1901
_facts: Wooded hill rising to 679 m overlooking Lake Zürich, east of the city
Zürich Zoo and FIFA headquarters are both located on the Zürichberg
Tram route 6, the Rigiblick funicular and the Dolderbahn rack railway all run up different parts of the hill
Rigiblick restaurant built in 1901 at the top

w: A red-brick factory in Wollishofen that left-wing campaigners fought to save from demolition and turn into a cultural centre instead - the 'Red Factory' name works on two levels, brick colour and politics both. It's now one of Zurich's main music and culture venues, still carrying the fight in its name.
s: The 'Red Factory' - brick colour and politics both
_facts: Former factory in the Wollishofen neighbourhood, now a music venue and cultural centre
Named for its red-brick buildings, but also because left-wing parties campaigned to turn it into a cultural centre

w: Switzerland's first purpose-built mosque, inaugurated in 1963 with the UN General Assembly's president presiding. Its foundation stone came from the Mubarak Mosque in India, laid in 1962 by the Ahmadiyya founder's own daughter - a sign of Muslim women's standing. Its minaret is a style Switzerland has since banned.
s: Switzerland's first mosque, and its last legal minaret
_facts: First purpose-built mosque in Switzerland, run by the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community
Foundation stone laid 25 August 1962 with a stone from the wall of the Mubarak Mosque, India, by Amatul Hafeez Begum, daughter of Ahmadiyya founder Mirza Ghulam Ahmad
Inaugurated 22 June 1963 by Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan, then president of the UN General Assembly, with Zurich mayor Emil Landolt present
Has a minaret; new minaret construction is now banned in Switzerland by popular vote

w: Opened in 1929, the first zoo in Europe to breed Galapagos tortoises successfully, sending offspring to two dozen other zoos. In 2005 keepers realised seven 'mouse lemurs' here were an undescribed species. In July 2020 a Siberian tiger mauled a keeper to death in front of visitors - its darkest headline yet.
s: Tortoise pioneers, a new lemur species, one dark headline
_facts: Opened 1929, third oldest zoo in Switzerland, located in the Fluntern quarter
Only/first European institution to successfully breed Galápagos tortoises, sending babies to more than two dozen other zoos
In 2005 discovered seven lemurs thought to be mouse lemurs were a new species, later named Goodman's mouse lemur
In July 2020 a Siberian tiger mauled a zookeeper to death in front of members of the public
